findings.title: Dirty-set race condition drops re-dirtied nodes during concurrent maintenance refresh
findings.evidence: crates/clio-write/src/memtree_maint.rs:117-136, 175-201, 230-236: `snapshot_dirty` reads `dirty_set` without clearing it; `enqueue_dirty` rejects nodes already present as duplicates; `refresh_one` unconditionally clears `n.dirty = false` without checking `n.generation`; and `drain_dirty` removes the node from `dirty_set` at the end of the wave, discarding any dirty marks enqueued while refresh was running.
findings.recommendation: Drain dirty IDs on wave snapshot, compare `node.generation` before setting `dirty = false` in `refresh_one`, and do not remove nodes from `dirty_set` whose generation counter increased after the wave began.

findings.title: Roadmap isolation rule violated by explicit 'Phase 100060' references in clio-write code and comments
findings.evidence: crates/clio-write/src/memtree.rs:71 ('/// Inputs for attaching a Phase 100060 leaf into the tree.') and crates/clio-write/src/memtree_maint.rs:12 ('//! - `MaintenanceHook` that attaches Phase 100060 leaves into the forest').
findings.requirement_ref: AGENTS.md Hard rules ('Roadmap isolation: never reference ./roadmap/, phase numbers, or roadmap files from code or comments'), roadmap/phase-100070-memtree-dirty-path-maintenance.md Hard rules
findings.recommendation: Remove all mentions of 'Phase 100060' from docstrings and module headers, replacing them with generic domain terminology (e.g. 'canonical leaf' or 'ingest leaf').

findings.title: Same-depth parallel refresh spawns unbounded OS threads and fully serializes on coarse-grained forest Mutex
findings.evidence: crates/clio-write/src/memtree_maint.rs:168-179 spawns an unbounded `thread::scope` worker per dirty node at the current depth with no concurrency cap, violating the bounded concurrency mandate (`min(P, num_dirty_at_level)`). Each worker immediately calls `refresh_one`, which locks `forest` (`Arc<Mutex<MemForest>>`) across the entire summary recomputation and interval adjustment, serializing all threads.
findings.requirement_ref: requirement.md §4.3 Step 5, roadmap/phase-100070-memtree-dirty-path-maintenance.md §5 Task 3, §6 Agent Decision Boundary
findings.recommendation: Introduce a bounded worker pool / semaphore matching CPU budget P, and narrow lock acquisition so child data is read snapshot-style and summary formatting runs outside the forest write lock.

findings.title: Newly added Rust test modules omit mandatory AGENTS.md responsibility header blocks
findings.evidence: crates/clio-store/src/memtree_persist_tests.rs:1-3, crates/clio-store/src/postgres_ext_tests.rs:1-3, crates/clio-write/src/memtree_tests.rs:1-3, and crates/clio-write/src/memtree_cov_tests.rs:1-3 contain only copyright notices and omit `//! # Responsibility`, `//! ## Owns`, `//! ## Does not own`, and `//! ## Boundary`.
findings.recommendation: Prepend the standard 4-section module responsibility header template to all 4 test files.

findings.title: Acceptance test T100070-10 / AC-100070-07 is fudged and does not test MemoryItem snapshot safety against summary refresh
findings.evidence: crates/clio-write/src/memtree_tests.rs:268-300 (`t10_summary_does_not_mutate_leaf_gist`) verifies only that an in-memory `summary_gist` string on an `AttachLeaf` is preserved across ancestor refresh. It constructs no `MemoryItem`, exercises no structured `snapshot` payload, and performs no assertion against snapshot bytes.
findings.recommendation: Update T100070-10 to attach an actual `MemoryItem` with structured `snapshot` bytes through `LeafIndex`, execute ancestor refresh, and assert that `LeafIndex::get` / `get_snapshot` returns byte-identical snapshot content.

findings.title: Internal node interval_end calculation truncates during k-ary split
findings.evidence: crates/clio-write/src/memtree_attach.rs:209-216 computes `sibling.interval_end` as `last.interval_end`, where `last` is the child with the greatest `interval_start`. If an earlier child in the sibling partition has a longer duration (`interval_end > last.interval_end`), the sibling interval is truncated and `refresh_interval_from_children` is never called on the sibling, corrupting time-range query filters.
findings.recommendation: Call `self.refresh_interval_from_children(&sibling_id)` after creating the sibling node in `split_upwards` to compute the true max `interval_end` across all assigned children.

findings.title: Migration updates schema_settings version to 3 before validating table reshape, risking corrupted metadata
findings.evidence: crates/clio-store/src/sqlite.rs:49-52 and crates/clio-store/src/postgres.rs:27-30 execute `SQL_CORE` (which updates `schema_version = '3'`) before invoking `ensure_memtree_shape_sqlite` / `ensure_memtree_shape_pg`. If `memtree_nodes` has existing rows, the function errors with `ConfigCorrupt`, but the schema version remains stamped as 3.
findings.recommendation: Run `ensure_memtree_shape` before `SQL_CORE` or decouple `schema_settings` version update from `SQL_CORE` so the version is only bumped after all reshape checks succeed.

findings.title: MemTree persistence in clio-store is disconnected from clio-write orchestration and lacks durable lifecycle integration
findings.evidence: crates/clio-write/Cargo.toml:10-18 lacks an `clio-store` dependency despite `crates.md:49`. `MemForest` is purely in-memory; `clio-store` CRUD methods (`upsert_memtree_node`, etc.) are only called in store unit tests and never during leaf ingest or maintenance.
findings.recommendation: Clarify durable vs in-process MemTree lifecycle boundaries in downstream phases or wire store persistence behind an optional/async sink in `MemTreeMaint`.

findings.title: Test t06 does not verify non-blocking write behavior during active maintenance refresh
findings.evidence: crates/clio-write/src/memtree_tests.rs:173-207 (`t06_consolidate_nonblocking_with_writes`) calls `consolidate_tool` with 3 nodes which completes instantly, then joins a thread calling `attach_leaf` directly rather than through `MaintenanceHook::on_leaf_attached`. It does not exercise concurrent write arrival while a refresh is in-flight.
findings.recommendation: Add a test with a blocking or slow refresh worker that proves leaf ingestion returns with sub-millisecond latency while a refresh wave is actively executing.

subject: Clio Phase 100070 (MemTree and Dirty-Path Maintenance)
verdict_justification: While basic in-memory MemTree insertion and dual-backend CRUD tests pass, critical data race conditions in dirty-set maintenance drop re-dirtied nodes under concurrent writes, violating §4.3 Step 4. Furthermore, code comments violate the roadmap isolation hard rule, four new test files omit required responsibility headers, parallel refresh serializes on a coarse-grained lock with unbounded OS threads, and acceptance criterion T100070-10 was fudged without testing snapshot safety.
standard: FR-3 / PR-9: Leaf readability preserved; construction and structural maintenance are separate, non-blocking processes.
§4.3 Steps 3–5: MemTree hierarchical temporal index, dirty-path ancestor marking, and level-parallel refresh.
PR-4: Structured snapshot fidelity preserved; ancestor summaries are non-authoritative and must never mutate snapshots.
AGENTS.md: Hard rules on roadmap isolation, 450-line maximum per file, and strict file header structure.
Coverage gate: ≥90% line and function coverage workspace aggregate and on every reported Rust source file.

issues.title: Dirty-set race condition drops re-dirtied nodes during concurrent maintenance refresh
issues.why_it_matters: When leaves are attached concurrently with background maintenance refresh, any ancestor marked dirty during an in-flight refresh wave is either cleared despite unsummarized changes or removed from dirty_set while still dirty in memory. In both cases, the node will never be refreshed by subsequent maintenance waves.
issues.impact: Data loss in ancestor summaries; stale or permanently dirty MemTree state under the primary non-blocking write scenario.
issues.evidence: crates/clio-write/src/memtree_maint.rs:117-136, 175-201, 230-236: snapshot_dirty clones without draining; enqueue_dirty rejects re-insertions as duplicates; refresh_one unconditionally sets dirty = false; and drain_dirty removes nodes from dirty_set even if generation bumped.
issues.proposed_fix: Drain dirty IDs on wave snapshot, compare node.generation before setting dirty = false in refresh_one, and do not remove nodes from dirty_set whose generation counter increased after the wave began.

issues.title: Roadmap isolation rule violated by explicit 'Phase 100060' references in clio-write
issues.why_it_matters: The codebase must remain fully functional and decoupled if the roadmap/ directory is deleted. Hard rules in AGENTS.md strictly forbid mentioning phase numbers in code or comments.
issues.impact: Breaks architectural isolation and violates repository hard rules.
issues.evidence: crates/clio-write/src/memtree.rs:71 ('/// Inputs for attaching a Phase 100060 leaf into the tree.') and crates/clio-write/src/memtree_maint.rs:12 ('//! - `MaintenanceHook` that attaches Phase 100060 leaves into the forest').
issues.proposed_fix: Remove all mentions of 'Phase 100060' from docstrings and module headers, replacing them with generic domain terminology (e.g. 'canonical leaf' or 'ingest leaf').

issues.title: Same-depth parallel refresh spawns unbounded OS threads and fully serializes on coarse-grained forest Mutex
issues.why_it_matters: Spawning an OS thread per dirty node at the current level without bounding violates the min(P, num_dirty_at_level) mandate and risks thread starvation or memory exhaustion on wide trees. Furthermore, holding forest.lock() inside refresh_one across the entire child read and summary generation serializes all worker threads, negating parallel speedup.
issues.impact: Unbounded resource usage and zero actual concurrency during level refresh.
issues.evidence: crates/clio-write/src/memtree_maint.rs:168-179 spawns unbounded thread::scope workers; line 214 locks forest across the entire execution of refresh_one.
issues.proposed_fix: Bound worker concurrency to pool budget P, read child summaries under a brief read lock, and perform string aggregation outside the forest write lock.

issues.title: Newly added Rust test modules omit mandatory AGENTS.md responsibility header blocks
issues.why_it_matters: AGENTS.md mandates that every Rust source file use the standard 4-section responsibility header template. Omitting this in test modules degrades architectural clarity and violates workspace standards.
issues.impact: Non-compliance with AGENTS.md file header constraints.
issues.proposed_fix: Prepend the standard 4-section module responsibility header template to all 4 test files.

issues.title: Acceptance test T100070-10 / AC-100070-07 is fudged and does not test MemoryItem snapshot safety against summary refresh
issues.why_it_matters: AC-100070-07 and PR-4 require verification that derived ancestor summaries never mutate or corrupt authoritative MemoryItem structured snapshots. Verifying an in-memory summary_gist string on an un-attached leaf is a vacuous check.
issues.impact: Fudged acceptance criterion leaves PR-4 snapshot fidelity unverified.
issues.evidence: crates/clio-write/src/memtree_tests.rs:268-300 (t10_summary_does_not_mutate_leaf_gist) asserts equality only on leaf_node.summary_gist; no MemoryItem snapshot is constructed or verified.
issues.proposed_fix: Update T100070-10 to attach an actual MemoryItem with structured snapshot bytes through LeafIndex, execute ancestor refresh, and assert that LeafIndex::get / get_snapshot returns byte-identical snapshot content.

issues.title: Internal node interval_end calculation truncates during k-ary split
issues.why_it_matters: During node split, sibling.interval_end is set to last.interval_end. If a non-last child in the partition has a later interval_end, the sibling internal node's interval is truncated, causing time-range queries to omit relevant ancestor nodes.
issues.impact: Incorrect time-range query filtering in memtree_query.
issues.evidence: crates/clio-write/src/memtree_attach.rs:209-216 assigns last.interval_end without checking whether earlier children in right_ids have greater interval_end.
issues.proposed_fix: Call self.refresh_interval_from_children(&sibling_id) after creating the sibling node in split_upwards.

issues.title: Migration updates schema_settings version to 3 before validating table reshape, risking corrupted metadata
issues.why_it_matters: If an existing store with pre-existing memtree_nodes rows fails migration in ensure_memtree_shape_sqlite / ensure_memtree_shape_pg, the database is stamped with schema_version = '3' even though the table lacks required interval columns.
issues.impact: Corrupted schema_settings metadata on migration error.
issues.evidence: crates/clio-store/src/sqlite.rs:49-52 and crates/clio-store/src/postgres.rs:27-30 run SQL_CORE before table validation.
issues.proposed_fix: Validate table shape before running SQL_CORE or decouple version bumping so schema_settings is only updated when all validations pass.

issues.title: MemTree persistence in clio-store is disconnected from clio-write orchestration and lacks durable lifecycle integration
issues.why_it_matters: clio-write has no dependency on clio-store and runs MemForest purely in-memory. Persistent tables in SQLite/Postgres remain unpopulated by the write path and tree state is lost on process restart.
issues.impact: MemTree data is not durable across host restarts.
issues.evidence: crates/clio-write/Cargo.toml lacks clio-store dependency; store CRUD methods are only called in clio-store unit tests.
issues.proposed_fix: Clarify durable vs in-process MemTree lifecycle boundaries in downstream phases or wire store persistence behind an optional/async sink in MemTreeMaint.

issues.title: Test t06 does not verify non-blocking write behavior during active maintenance refresh
issues.why_it_matters: t06 completes consolidate immediately on 3 nodes and joins a thread calling attach_leaf directly rather than testing writes during active refresh.
issues.impact: Acceptance criterion AC-100070-05 is weakly verified.
issues.evidence: crates/clio-write/src/memtree_tests.rs:173-207 uses instant refresh and bypasses MaintenanceHook on concurrent write.
issues.proposed_fix: Add a test with a slow/blocking refresh worker proving leaf writes succeed without delay during an in-flight refresh wave.
